headline: Youth remanded for 7 days over 'sniper' comment on PM's visit
summary: A college student from Rajshahi is in custody after posting a Facebook comment suggesting a sniper attack on a bus used by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
details: A Dhaka court has granted police seven days to question Abu Bakar Siddique in custody. The second-year honours student from New Government Degree College in Rajshahi was arrested over a social media post.
The arrest followed a Facebook comment made by Abu Bakar on a photo of a bus used by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman during his visit to Rajshahi on October 20.
The comment, posted on a page called 'The Beauty of Rajshahi', read: 'Ah! There was a big opportunity. The only thing missing was a sniper.'
The suspect told the court that he made the comment 'as a joke' and 'casually' with no intention of harm.
However, prosecution argued that the comment cannot be dismissed as an ordinary post and suggested a possible conspiracy to assassinate the prime minister.
Abu Bakar was detained by the Special Response Battalion (SRB) from his home in the Kachuatail area of Rajshahi on Wednesday night.
A case has been filed against him under the Anti-Terrorism Act, and police are investigating whether others are involved in the poiché
The prime minister had traveled by a RUET bus to visit puja pavilions and attend a rally at Madrasa Maidan during his Rajshahi visit.

headline_marked: Bay depression [[may develop into cyclone]] Arnab
headline: Bay depression may develop into cyclone Arnab
summary: The Bangladesh Meteorological Department warns of a potential very severe cyclonic storm heading towards India's coast.
details: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified and could develop into a cyclone on Monday, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department.
If the system strengthens, it will be named 'Arnab', a name proposed by Bangladesh meaning ocean or sea.
The depression is currently centred 810km south of Chattogram Port, 730km south of Cox's Bazar Port, 850km south of Mongla Port, and 780km south of Payra Port.
The system is expected to move north-westwards and may eventually cross India's Andhra coast as a very severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday.
Maximum sustained winds near the centre are reaching 50km per hour, with gusts or squalls of up to 60km per hour, causing rough seas.
Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been advised to keep hoisting distant warning Signal No. 1.
All fishing boats and trawlers in the northern Bay of Bengal have been instructed to move closer to the coast and navigate with caution.
caption:
A deep depression in the Bay of Bengal is intensifying and could soon become a cyclone named Arnab.

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal has intensified and could develop into a cyclone on Monday, according to the Bangladesh Meteorological Department.

If the system strengthens, it will be named 'Arnab', a name proposed by Bangladesh meaning ocean or sea.

The depression is currently centred 810km south of Chattogram Port, 730km south of Cox's Bazar Port, 850km south of Mongla Port, and 780km south of Payra Port.

The system is expected to move north-westwards and may eventually cross India's Andhra coast as a very severe cyclonic storm by Wednesday.

Maximum sustained winds near the centre are reaching 50km per hour, with gusts or squalls of up to 60km per hour, causing rough seas.

Chattogram, Cox's Bazar, Mongla, and Payra ports have been advised to keep hoisting distant warning Signal No. 1.

All fishing boats and trawlers in the northern Bay of Bengal have been instructed to move closer to the coast and navigate with caution.
